title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 53–56). We work over a base S on which 2 is invertible. E/S is an elliptic curve and V = E[2], an étale group scheme locally isomorphic to (Z/2)^2. The curve X = E/{±1} is a genus-0 curve (a P^1-bundle) carrying the residual translation action of V. Inside X sits I, the image of E[2]: a V-orbit of 4 points, which is a V-torsor.

The octahedral structure. Each nonzero t in V acts on X as an involution. Its fixed points are the images of the P with 2P = t, which gives 2 points on X. The three involutions therefore fix 6 points in total (the 'octahedron'). The quotient X/V is again a genus-0 curve, branched at 3 points with ramification index 2. Those 3 points are indexed by the degree-3 étale cover J of nonzero elements (J ≅ V*\{0}).

The 'standard model' (12). Over J one takes the line Σ_J : Σ_{i∈J} y_i = 0 in P(O^J), with the divisor D_J = {y_i = 0}, which has degree 3, and sets Σ*_J = Σ_J \ D_J. Over it one takes the conic C_J : Σ_{i∈J} x_i^2 = 0, with the map y_i = x_i^2. The group V_J = (μ_2)^J/μ_2 ≅ F_2^J/F_2 acts diagonally by sign changes on the x_i. C_J → Σ_J is a Galois V_J-cover branched exactly over D_J with index 2. Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g − 2 = 4(−2) + 3·2, so g = 0, which checks.

Since H^1(P^1 − 3 points, Z/2) ≅ (Z/2)^2, the restriction over Σ*_J is the universal abelian exponent-2 cover Σ*_{J,2}, i.e. the pro-2 abelianized π_1 cover mod 2. This is the 'NB' on p. 54.

The equivalence. The data (X, I) are therefore equivalent to:
- (i) the degree-3 cover J, equivalently the twisted marked line (Σ_J, D_J);
- (ii) a V_J-torsor K, which recovers X* = K ∧_{V_J} Σ*_{J,2} as in formula (11), with the admissibility condition that the induced map V_J → V_J is the identity;
- (iii) a section x of Σ*_J/S, the image of the origin, i.e. the 'point at infinity'. This image lies off the branch locus because the orbit I is free.

The margin relation (14) ties these together: I ≅ K ∧ (fibre of Σ*_{J,2} over x), as made explicit in (16) on the next page. Hence, given J and I, both x and K are determined up to the evident ambiguity. The elliptic curve itself is recovered as the double cover of X branched along I.

Rigidified case. With level structure (I and J constant, epinglage), Σ*_J is the fixed curve P^1 − {3 points}, K is fixed, and the datum reduces to a section x ∈ Σ*_J(S). This identifies the level-2 moduli with P^1 − {0, 1, ∞}, i.e. the Legendre λ-line, in an intrinsic, S_3-equivariant, descent-friendly form.

The margins indicate how to describe Σ_J and the conic for nonconstant J. Σ_J is the projectivized trace-zero part of the cubic étale algebra Ω_J, with equation L(u) = Tr(u) = 0. The conic is given by a trace quadratic form Q(u∧v) = Tr(...). There is a mention, apparently of 'Anderson'.

Purpose: a stack-theoretic presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] (curves in char ≠ 2) via Klein-four-group-equivariant genus-0 curves. It is a step toward describing the moduli of elliptic curves and its π_1 in terms of P^1 minus 3 points (anabelian / Teichmüller-tower motivations).
errors: Minor notational point: V_J ≃ F_2^J/F_2 should be read as (μ_2)^J modulo the diagonal μ_2, which acts trivially on the projective conic. This is consistent and not an error.
On the line 'Σ*_J = Σ_J' in the constant case: probably intended as Σ*_J ≅ (Σ_J)_S constant, or 'Σ*_J ⊂ Σ_J also fixed'. As literally transcribed, Σ* = Σ is false, since D_J is removed.
The relation (14) is only sketched in the margin; completeness of the equivalence (that the double cover branched at I recovers E with its origin) is asserted, not checked, on this page.

ideas.what: Klein-four cover of P^1 by the conic Σx_i^2 = 0 over Σy_i = 0, branched at 3 points: the universal Z/2-abelian cover of P^1 minus 3 points
ideas.modern_name: Fermat-type conic / maximal elementary abelian 2-cover of P^1 − {0, 1, ∞}

ideas.what: Elliptic curve with E[2] ↔ (degree-3 étale cover J, V-torsor K, section of the twisted P^1 − 3 points), via X = E/±1 with V-action (octahedral structure)
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] via Y(2) = P^1 − {0, 1, ∞} with S_3-descent; Legendre form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre/classical; stack version folklore (e.g. Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur style level-2 moduli)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and P^1 − 3 points but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Twisted form of the marked line via the trace-zero hyperplane of a cubic étale algebra, and the conic via a trace quadratic form
ideas.modern_name: Twisted forms of (P^1, 3 points) classified by étale cubic algebras; trace form conic

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, base-independent (descent-theoretic) version of the classical Legendre/level-2 description of elliptic curves via the Klein four-group acting on E/±1. It is elegant but its content is known in the literature on level-2 moduli; no new result or unrecognized connection is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'des torseurs K sur V_J' should read 'des torseurs K sous V_J'.
Margin: 'description valable localement (cit)' (local description); the conic is described via P(p_*(Ω_J)) with trace forms.
Constant case: likely 'J ≃ J_S, et Σ*_J ≃ (Σ*_J)_S est aussi fixé' rather than 'Σ*_J = Σ_J'.
'(V_J)_S = V(J_S) = V' (the group scheme associated with the constant J).
'(à fins d'épinglage)' = for the purpose of rigidification.
